findingDetails.title: Quoted executor forms bypass Pi dispatch inspection
findingDetails.evidence: directExecutor rejects any quoted executable token, and hasDispatchEvidence also excludes quoted executor tokens. inspectDispatch therefore returns kind none for a shell-equivalent command such as "devin" -p "task". matchDispatchShape delegates to inspectDispatch, while the Pi preflight exits immediately for kind none, so the command is neither authorized nor audited as a dispatch.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The producer is dispatch-audit.mjs:186-221 and 229-262; the consumers are the Pi preflight inspector path and the Pi audit adapter. The legacy DISPATCH_SHAPES entries still recognize the executor shape, but matchDispatchShape no longer evaluates those expressions.
findingDetails.recommendation: Preserve quote-safe executable normalization or classify quoted/path-qualified executor forms as ambiguous, then add inspectDispatch and registered Pi tool_call coverage for quoted and path-qualified executors.
findingDetails.claim: A user can execute a quoted external CLI through Pi Bash without the explicit-executor authorization check because the parser silently classifies the command as non-dispatch.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the Pi/Bash runtime rejects quoted executable tokens or whether another mandatory guard reclassifies kind none; the reviewed hook contract and factory tests provide no such constraint.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Rejecting quoted tokens may have been intended as conservative shell parsing, but quote removal is unambiguous for a standalone executable token and the earlier regex-based shape accepted the same form.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only if the upstream Pi Bash tool rejects quoted executable tokens before this hook or a separate mandatory guard covers them.

findingDetails.claim: Quoted executor forms are reduced to the first token and classified as known without validating the remaining shell fragment, so a quoted codex wrapper can evade Pi dispatch authorization and inspection.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A caller-side parser or a post-normalization check that rejects trailing shell syntax before the Pi authorization result is consumed.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The quoted form may be intended to represent a literal executable argument rather than shell syntax; that would reduce exploitability but still leaves the accepted command shape under-specified.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Demonstrate that every authorization consumer reparses the complete quoted command and rejects non-executable trailing fragments.

findingDetails.claim: A child that can write the receipt directory can forge a structurally valid intent/completion pair because receipt MAC mismatches are warnings, and the validator then treats route-proof fields as advisory.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: An OS-enforced parent-only receipt store, separate writer identity, or persisted run-bound verification key that makes a child-written receipt fail closed.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The process-local key may be intentionally limited to same-process correlation, with structural facts considered sufficient when the caller guarantees the receipt directory is inaccessible to the child. The in-scope API relies on that guarantee rather than enforcing it.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Show that all workspace-write dispatch callers place receipts in a store the child cannot write and that MAC failure is blocking on every route-proof relaxation path.

findingDetails.claim: Write containment can miss a child mutation of a pre-existing dirty path outside the artifact directory because the baseline and post-dispatch comparison store only path names and subtract any path already present in that baseline.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A content or index snapshot for pre-existing dirty paths, or an isolated worktree/OS boundary that prevents the leaf from touching those paths.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Path-only subtraction may intentionally preserve unrelated user or sibling changes; however, it cannot distinguish those changes from a child rewrite of the same path.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Demonstrate byte/hash or index-state comparison for every pre-existing out-of-scope path, or prove all affected dispatches run in an isolated worktree.

findingDetails.title: Quoted executor forms bypass Pi dispatch inspection
findingDetails.claim: A quoted external executor can become non-dispatch before Pi authorization consumes the result.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: An upstream Pi/Bash rejection or separate mandatory guard for the complete command.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The parser may intentionally reject quoted executables, but that restriction is undocumented and the form is shell-equivalent.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only if upstream Pi rejects these tokens or another mandatory guard covers the complete command.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The producer is dispatch-audit.mjs:186-262 and consumers are Pi preflight and Pi audit; tests cover quoted payload text, not quoted executable tokens.
findingDetails.recommendation: Normalize quote-safe executables or classify them ambiguous, then add shared and registered-Pi coverage.

findingDetails.title: Receipt MAC failures are advisory at the route-proof boundary
findingDetails.claim: A child able to write receipts can forge a structurally valid intent/completion pair because MAC mismatch is warning-only.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: An OS-enforced parent-only receipt store or persisted verifier key that makes child-written receipts fail closed.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The process-local key may be intended only for same-process correlation, but receipt-directory isolation is not enforced here.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only if all callers use a child-inaccessible store and every MAC failure blocks route-proof relaxation.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The loader, pair validator, route-proof demotion, key derivation, and mismatched-MAC test form one chain.
findingDetails.recommendation: Use parent-authored or OS-protected receipts and fail closed when authentication is unavailable.

findingDetails.title: Dirty-path containment skips pre-existing paths by name
findingDetails.claim: Write containment can miss a child mutation of a pre-existing dirty path outside the artifact directory.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A content/hash or index snapshot for every pre-existing out-of-scope path, or isolated worktrees for all callers.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Path subtraction may preserve unrelated changes, but it cannot distinguish them from a child rewrite of the same path.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only after content/index comparison or isolation covers every caller.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The snapshot/detection producer and codex fanout caller share path-only exclusion semantics.
findingDetails.recommendation: Capture content or index fingerprints, or isolate the leaf so same-path mutations remain attributable.

findingDetails.title: Completion status reconciliation ignores open plan criteria and a failing strict gate
findingDetails.claim: The packet can publish Complete metadata while required completion evidence remains open.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A machine-enforced exception that plan rows are advisory and strict freshness exit 2 is non-gating.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Tasks/checklist plus generated metadata may intentionally be the only status authority, but that exception is not encoded in the status command.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only if the authoritative validator exits 0 or the repository contract mechanically exempts these states.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The status producer is reused across children, so omitted plan rows or stale strict freshness can be hidden by the same logic.
findingDetails.recommendation: Include plan criteria and strict freshness in the status gate, or make the exception explicit and machine-enforced.
